To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
trypsin was successfully immobilized on three different monolithic disks, and that a monolithic IMER was developed for rapid on-line digestion of proteins and PMF.
three trypsin IMERs were prepared by immobilization of trypsin on epoxy, CDI and EDA CIM monolithic disks and that the EDA-based IMER was the most efficient for on-line digestion.
the immobilization of trypsin on three monolithic supports (CIM epoxy, CDI and EDA) allows the on-line digestion of proteins with good repeatability and satisfactory stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of trypsin IMERs for rapid on-line protein digestions.
the preparation of a trypsin-based IMER that can be directly coupled to an LC-MS/MS system for the rapid and reliable on-line protein digestion of complex protein mixtures.
the development and optimization of trypsin IMERs for the digestion of proteins in flow-through conditions and the analysis of the obtained digests by mass spectrometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a trypsin IMER prepared on a glutaraldehyde-derivatized EDA-CIM monolithic disk was the best one in terms of immobilized trypin activity, on-line digestion efficiency and long-term stability.
the IMER based on trypsin immobilization on a glutaraldehyde-derivatized EDA-CIM disk is a suitable and robust tool for on-line protein identification by PMF.
the IMERs based on EDA and CDI monolithic disks are the most suitable for on-line protein digestions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a trypsin-based IMER was developed to perform rapid protein digestion and to be coupled to a LC-ESI- MS/MS system.
the use of monolithic IMERs for on-line protein digestions is a promising alternative to the conventional in-solution digestion.
the trypsin-based IMERs can be used for rapid on-line digestion of proteins and peptides and that the EDA-CIM-IMER is the best one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IMERs are suitable for rapid protein identification by PMF, which is an important step in proteomics.

the use of monolithic IMERs can be a valid alternative to in-solution digestion, especially for the analysis of complex protein mixtures, since it allows a fast, efficient and reproducible digestion of proteins in a single step.
